newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK airline will not fly Cambodian prince back home.
newsitem.headline: HK airline will not fly Cambodian prince back home.

text.p: Hong Kong's Dragonair airline said on Tuesday it would not fly Cambodia's exiled Prince Norodom Sirivudh to Phnom Penh after a warning by the government there that he would be arrested on arrival.
"Dragonair really has no alternative but to deny him boarding. He will not be allowed to board the flight," Dragonair spokesman John Bailey told Reuters in response to enquiries.

"The position now is that Dragonair has been notified officially by the Cambodian government that Prince Norodom (Sirivudh) will not be welcomed into Cambodia and he will not be allowed to enter Cambodia," Bailey said.
The prince, who arrived in Hong Kong from Frankfurt earlier on Tuesday, had already been told he would not be allowed to board, despite a prior reservation.

Sirivudh, former foreign minister and half brother of King Norodom Sihanouk, went into exile in December 1995 after being held for one month on charges of involvement in an alleged plot against the life of Second Prime Minister Hun Sen.
The exiled prince has denied the charges and has said he wants to return to seek justice.
